question: Which system changes caused the payment processing delays in March 2026, which services were affected, and which documents confirm this?
answer:
The March 2026 payment‑processing delays were traced to two separate system changes:

1. **Card‑payment delays (11 Mar 2026)** – Two changes combined to cause the incident:
   * **CHG‑2044** – rollout of fraud‑scoring model v3.3, which raised the fraud‑scoring p99 latency from ~80 ms to ~450 ms.
   * **CHG‑2041** – reduction of the payment‑gateway database connection pool from 200 to 60 connections.
   These changes led to time‑outs and queuing in several services: the **merchant‑api (Checkout API)**, **payment‑gateway**, **fraud‑scoring**, **notification‑service** (receipt/webhook backlog) and **settlement‑batch** (late nightly run) as well as the overall **Card payments** component[E4][E9].

2. **Receipt‑email and webhook delays (23‑24 Mar 2026)** – The delay was caused by **CHG‑2051**, a Kafka‑broker upgrade that created a consumer‑group rebalancing loop in the **notification‑service**, delaying receipt emails and merchant webhooks by up to three hours[E6][E3].

**Documents confirming the causes and affected services**:
* The final **Postmortem INC‑2026‑0311 – Card payment processing delays** (PDF) – details the two changes (CHG‑2044, CHG‑2041) and lists the affected services[E4][E9].
* The final **Incident Report INC‑2026‑0324 – Delayed payment notifications** (PDF) – identifies CHG‑2051 as the root cause and names the affected **notification‑service**[E6][E3].
* The Kestrel Pay status‑page incident entries for 11 Mar (delayed card payments) and 23‑24 Mar (delayed payment notifications) also record the affected components and the rollback of the risk‑scoring change[E1][E2].

citations.section: Postmortem INC-2026-0311 - Card payment processing delays > Summary
citations.text: Between 13:52 and 16:40 UTC on 2026-03-11, card payments were delayed or failed. Two changes combined to cause the incident. CHG-2044 rolled out fraud model v3.3, which raised fraud-scoring p99 latency from about 80 ms to about 450 ms. CHG-2041, made two days earlier, had reduced the payment-gateway database connection pool from 200 to 60 connections. Neither change caused problems on its own.

citations.section: Postmortem INC-2026-0311 - Card payment processing delays > Affected services
citations.text:
Service: merchant-api; Effect: Checkout requests timed out after 30 seconds (HTTP 504)

Service: payment-gateway; Effect: Requests queued waiting for a ledgerdb connection

Service: fraud-scoring; Effect: p99 latency rose to about 450 ms after CHG-2044

Service: notification-service; Effect: Receipt and webhook backlog, delayed up to 2 hours

Service: settlement-batch; Effect: Nightly run started 47 minutes late

citations.text: From 22:10 UTC on 2026-03-23 to 01:15 UTC on 2026-03-24, payment receipt emails and merchant webhooks were delayed by up to 3 hours. The cause was a consumer group rebalancing loop in notification-service after the Kafka broker upgrade CHG-2051.

question: When did the impact of INC-2026-0311 start?
answer: The impact of INC-2026-0311 began on 2026‑03‑11 at about 14:05 UTC (the incident was reported to have started at 14:05 UTC, with delays observed roughly from 14:00 UTC)[E2][E6].

citations.title: Incident Report INC-2026-0311 - Card payment processing delays
citations.section: Incident Report INC-2026-0311 - Card payment processing delays > Summary
citations.text: On 2026-03-11 card payments submitted through the Checkout API were delayed and some failed with timeout errors. The incident started at 14:05 UTC and was resolved at 16:40 UTC. Fraud-scoring latency was elevated after the fraud model v3.3 rollout earlier that day. The model was rolled back and the payment-gateway database connection pool was enlarged.
